result.note: Tests the June 2026 India–Nepal UPI–NPI remittance link: the Nepali system linked, the builders and settlement design, and UPI's overseas footprint.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, India and Nepal launched a peer-to-peer cross-border remittance link connecting India's UPI with which Nepali payment system?
questions.explain: The link launched on 6 June 2026 connects UPI with Nepal's National Payments Interface (NPI). It lets users send money instantly across the border through mobile apps and digital wallets.
questions.source: On 6 June, the two countries launched a peer-to-peer cross-border remittance link connecting India's UPI and Nepal's National Payments Interface (NPI), allowing users to send money instantly across the border through mobile apps and digital wallets.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–Nepal cross-border payment link launched in June 2026:
items: It was built by NPCI International Payments Limited and Nepal Clearing House Limited.
Transfers move directly between the two national payment systems without correspondent banks, enabling real-time settlement.
Like most of UPI's existing overseas arrangements, it is limited to merchant payments through QR codes.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: most earlier UPI arrangements abroad centre on QR-code merchant payments, but this link goes further and enables full person-to-person remittances. The main beneficiaries are Indian tourists and Nepali workers sending money home.
questions.source: Transfers move directly between the two national payment systems without correspondent banks or separate foreign exchange processes, enabling real-time settlement.

questions.prompt: As reported in June 2026, UPI was accepted in nine countries. Which one of the following countries was NOT among them?
questions.explain: The nine countries listed are Singapore, the UAE, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka and Cambodia, so Malaysia is not among them. Most of these arrangements centre on merchant payments through QR codes.
questions.source: UPI is already accepted in nine countries, including Singapore, United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka and Cambodia.
